newsitem.title: UK: Celltech sees progress on Merck, Zeneca drugs.
newsitem.headline: Celltech sees progress on Merck, Zeneca drugs.

text.p: British drug discovery company Celltech Group Plc said late on Tuesday that it hoped to make progress this year on key collaborations with industry giants Merck & Co and Zeneca Group Plc.
Celltech was hit badly last February after Merck dropped development of a compound for asthma, while little news has emerged of a tie-up with Zeneca on a new class of drugs known as MMP inhibitors.
In an interview with Reuters, finance director Peter Allen said "I think the hope is that in 1997 Zeneca and Merck will identify development compounds or be very close to them."

Shares across the UK biotech sector were hit early last year when Merck said it was dropping CDP 840, a PDE IV inhibitor, because it did not represent a sufficient therapeutic advance over existing asthma products. Industry sources said at the time that Merck would only pursue a drug which could achieve annual sales approaching $1 billion.

Chief executive Peter Fellner told Reuters that since then scientists had been "working very heavily with a whole series of potential second-generation compounds that are very closely related to CDP 840. The aim has been to get drugs which are more potent or have a faster onset of action."
Fellner added: "We have a number of compounds that look quite interesting and we hope that ... in the first half of this year we will be able to identify possible development candidates."
The chief executive told Reuters that the chosen candidate would need to show "clear advantages over CDP 840 and potential advantages over compounds working by other mechanisms."
Fellner said the focus of Zeneca's interest in MMP inhibitors, the same class of drug as British Biotech Plc's anti-cancer agent Marimastat, had shifted away from cancer towards osteoarthritis.
"There is still an interest in oncology, but the whole thrust of the programme is really now focused on osteoarthritis, and we are making quite a lot of progress."
He added: "We hope within the next year or so to identify the lead compounds to evaluate. Zeneca are actually putting quite a large resource into it."

Osteoarthritis is a huge potential market, Fellner said, with around five million sufferers in Britain compared with one million rheumatoid arthritis patients. The condition is currently poorly treated.

Fellner said "90 percent" of the joint effort is targetted at osteoporosis, although both companies are watching to see if British Biotech has a successful cancer drug on its hands in Marimastat, now entering late-stage trials.
"I think if it begins to look as if they do then Zeneca might well be back into the oncology area," Fellner said.
Fellner told Reuters that prospects for another product which uses a Celltech antibody, a severe allergic asthma drug being developed by Schering-Plough Corp, are uncertain.
The Schering-Plough drug, which was featured prominently in Celltech's 1995 report and accounts, has been poised to enter clinical trials for around a year but has been delayed by safety concerns.
